focus: a complete KTZ-style dependency chain ending in one global polynomial and exponent $1-o(1)$

messages.body_markdown: Please target `E2E-07`, compatible with `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY`: preserve $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ accepted mass and obtain a rank-reaching family with $D\le A_\theta d\epsilon^{-\theta/(1-\theta)}$. The stronger interface $D=O_\theta(d)$ would discharge `E2E-14` automatically. The direct-decoder alternative is essential because the exact cover obstruction forbids universal graph-only sparsification.
messages.subject: Rank-or-decode interface

messages.body_markdown: Can `AE-19` be sharpened to prove `E2E-14` after the exact whole-$B$ cleanup? The needed conclusion is either an immediate decoder or one factor with mass $\mu_i=\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ and $4\Delta_i<\mu_i(p+1)$. Since `E2E-08` makes $D\ll\epsilon p$, the accepted whole-relation cleanup may remove the pending factorwise-polar lemma from this critical path.
messages.subject: Heavy-factor dichotomy

messages.body_markdown: Please formalize `E2E-16`: more than $\Delta$ compatible directions through one simple root should make the Newton lift truncate to $Q$, give $C(X,Y,Q)=0$, and hence force irreducible $C\sim Z-Q$. This would aggregate every $C$-class edge across disconnected components. The accepted P8 proves component-level lifting but not this global factor-linearization statement.
messages.subject: Vinh-free factor lift

messages.body_markdown: Do not conflate the fixed-$\eta$ target with an exact or arbitrarily fast varying exponent-one endpoint. The modal $d=101$ construction refutes a uniform $C(d/p)$ trigger with linear recovery, while the accepted component package independently stops at a square-root floor. Neither obstruction refutes any fixed $(d/p)^{1-\eta}$ theorem.
messages.subject: Endpoint guardrail

nodes.label: Bivariate test instance
nodes.notes: The scope is exactly $m=2$, prime field, and $100<d<p$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and a polynomial $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$ for every affine line $L$. Put $$\rho=\frac dp,\qquad \epsilon=\Pr_{L,\,x\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)],$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg_{\mathrm{tot}}Q\le d}\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)].$$

nodes.label: Accepted graph and completion predicate
nodes.notes: Edge mass and point agreement use compatible normalizations.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $$G_{\mathrm{acc}}=(\mathbb F_p^2,\mathcal L_p,E_{\mathrm{acc}}),\qquad E_{\mathrm{acc}}=\{(x,L):x\in L,\ P_L(x)=f(x)\}.$$ For $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq G_{\mathrm{acc}}$, define $$e(G)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)}.$$ For $c>0$, let $\mathsf{Done}_c$ denote the assertion that some $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c\epsilon$.

nodes.label: Fixed-eta reduction
nodes.notes: It suffices to build the quantitative engine for $0<\theta\le1/4$.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $\eta>0$, set $$\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}.$$ Then $0<\theta\le1/4$ and, since $0<\rho<1$, $$\rho^{1-\eta}\ge\rho^{1-\theta}.$$

nodes.label: Algebra-ready accepted core
nodes.notes: This is the incidence-to-algebra interface.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For $a>0$, an $(\epsilon,a)$-core is an accepted subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$ satisfying $$e(G)\ge a\epsilon,
\qquad
\min_{v\in X\sqcup T}\deg_G(v)\ge\lfloor a\epsilon p\rfloor.$$

nodes.label: Constant-loss popularity pruning
nodes.notes: The source step was individually judged valid, but its enclosing audit verdict is `revise`; the harness determines status.
nodes.statement_markdown:
The full accepted graph contains a subgraph $G_0$ with $$e(G_0)\ge\epsilon/4,
\qquad
\operatorname{mindeg}(G_0)\ge\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor.$$ In particular, $G_0$ is an $(\epsilon,1/100)$-core.

nodes.label: Rank-reaching family
nodes.notes: Actual constraint rank replaces the cardinality of the selected line family.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For $D\ge d$, let $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\},
\qquad N_d(D)=\dim V_D,$$ and, for $R\subseteq T$, define $$\Phi_{R,D}(A)=\bigl(A(M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$ Also define $$\operatorname{Reach}_{G,R}(L)=\{x:(x,L)\in E,\ \exists M\in R\setminus\{L\}\text{ with }(x,M)\in E\}.$$ The tuple $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching when $$R\subseteq T,
\quad |R|>D,
\quad \operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<N_d(D),
\quad |\operatorname{Reach}_{G,R}(L)|>D\ \text{ for every }L\in T.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal incidence/rank bottleneck. It imports the shared ideas `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY` and `AE-18`.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$ there exist $C_\theta,A_\theta,a_\theta>0$ such that, if $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\rho^{1-\theta},$$ then either $\mathsf{Done}_{a_\theta}$ holds, or $G_0$ contains $G=(X,T,E)$ and there are $R\subseteq T$ and an integer $D$ such that $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad d\le D\le A_\theta d\epsilon^{-\theta/(1-\theta)},$$ and $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching.

nodes.label: Near-linear exponent gate
nodes.notes: This is the exact parameter identity producing exponent $1-\theta$; it imposes no hidden condition such as $p\ge d^C$.
nodes.statement_markdown: In the relation alternative of `E2E-07`, $$\frac{D}{\epsilon p}\le A_\theta\frac{\rho}{\epsilon^{1/(1-\theta)}}\le A_\theta C_\theta^{-1/(1-\theta)}.$$ Hence $C_\theta$ may be chosen so that $$D<\frac{a_\theta\epsilon p}{10^4}<p.$$ If the displayed trigger exceeds $1$, the implication is simply vacuous.

nodes.label: Low-rank squarefree interpolant
nodes.notes: P3 supplies the interpolation, squarefree, and $Z$-dependence template; the rank-form restatement still needs an exact formalization.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If the relation alternative holds, there is a nonzero minimum-weight squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\quad(M\in R),
\qquad A_Z\not\equiv0.$$ Indeed, the rank inequality gives a kernel element, $|R|>D$ excludes a $Z$-independent element, and $D<p$ makes formal $Z$-differentiation nonzero.

nodes.label: Reached-root extension
nodes.notes: Ordinary root counting incurs no averaging loss.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every line vertex $L\in T$, $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Characteristic-safe whole-relation cleanup
nodes.notes: Using the accepted whole-$B$ bound avoids dependence on the pending factorwise-polar claim.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=hB$, where $h\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient gcd in $Z$. Then $B$ is primitive in $Z$, squarefree, and has degree below $p$. There is a formal directional derivative $\mathcal D$ with $\gcd(B,\mathcal DB)=1$ and an exceptional edge set satisfying $$|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$ Outside $E_{\mathrm{exc}}$, the line identities for $B$ hold and $\mathcal DB$ is nonzero at accepted points.

nodes.label: Global clean simple-root core
nodes.notes: This replaces the component-local $k^2\gtrsim dp$ calculation by the direct bound $D\ll\epsilon p$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
The normalized exceptional loss satisfies $$\frac{|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|}{p^2(p+1)}\le\left(\frac Dp\right)^2+ rac Dp=o_{C_\theta}(\epsilon).$$ After exceptional deletion and peeling, there are $b_\theta>0$ and a nonempty graph $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ such that $$e(G_1)\ge b_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad \operatorname{mindeg}(G_1)>D,$$ every line vertex satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and every point vertex satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Simple-root factor partition
nodes.notes: This is an elementary UFD and product-derivative step; it is the list produced by the algebraic relation.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Factor $$B=c\prod_{i=1}^s C_i$$ into distinct irreducible factors and put $\Delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_i)$. Every $C_i$ depends on $Z$, and $$s\le\deg_ZB\le\frac Dd\le A_\theta\epsilon^{-\theta/(1-\theta)}.$$ The vertices and edges of $G_1$ partition uniquely into factor classes $G_{1,i}$ such that $$C_i(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0,
\qquad C_i(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\ne0$$ on the corresponding line and point vertices. Writing $\mu_i=e(G_{1,i})$, one has $\sum_i\mu_i=e(G_1)$.

nodes.label: Heavy factor or cross-factor decoder
nodes.notes: This is the single-polynomial/list-collapse bottleneck, matching the shared algebraic node `AE-19`.
nodes.statement_markdown:
There exists $c_\theta>0$ such that every factor partition from `E2E-13` satisfies one of the following: $\mathsf{Done}_{c_\theta}$ holds, or some factor class obeys $$\mu_i\ge c_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad 4\Delta_i<\mu_i(p+1).$$

nodes.label: High-direction factor seed
nodes.notes: This averaging step replaces affine component mixing.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the factor alternative of `E2E-14`, some point $x$ is incident to more than $\Delta_i$ distinct lines of $G_{1,i}$. At that point, $$C_i(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Factor linearization
nodes.notes: The accepted source proves component-level Newton lifting. The irreducible-factor linearization and cross-component aggregation require a fresh exact proof.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $C=C_i$ and $\Delta=\Delta_i$. More than $\Delta$ compatible graph directions through the simple root in `E2E-15` determine a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$C(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0.$$ Since $C$ is irreducible and depends on $Z$, $$C\sim Z-Q.$$

nodes.label: All factor edges charge to one polynomial
nodes.notes: This is the explicit list-to-single conversion and uses no connectivity or Vinh estimate.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every point vertex $x$ of $G_{1,i}$, $C_i(x,f(x))=0$ and $C_i\sim Z-Q$ imply $Q(x)=f(x)$. Moreover, $$\frac{|X_{1,i}|}{p^2}\ge\frac{|E_{1,i}|}{p^2(p+1)}=\mu_i.$$ Thus either branch of `E2E-14` yields $\mathsf{Done}_{c_\theta}$.

nodes.label: Close every fixed eta
nodes.notes: Only monotonicity of $\rho^a$ on $0<\rho<1$ is used.
nodes.statement_markdown: Apply the chain with $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. Since $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\rho^{1-\eta}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\epsilon\ge C_\eta\rho^{1-\theta},$$ the $\theta$-theorem yields one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with agreement at least $c_\eta\epsilon$ for every fixed $\eta>0$.

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate soundness
nodes.notes: Blocked on `E2E-07`, `E2E-14`, and exact formalization of `E2E-16`. No work state is a proof-status claim.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, every $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and every degree-at-most-$d$ affine-line table, $$\operatorname{Agr}_{\mathrm{LVP}}(f,P)\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies that there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\operatorname{Agr}_{\mathrm{LVP}}(f,P).$$

nodes.label: Accepted component decoder package
nodes.notes: This exact accepted package ends in one polynomial, not a list.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If a connected accepted subgraph has minimum degree $k$ and line measure $\tau$ satisfying $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,
\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then some $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Current square-root frontier
nodes.notes: This is a method ceiling, not an impossibility theorem.
nodes.statement_markdown: If a pruned component additionally has $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon$, the accepted package gives one polynomial at agreement at least $\epsilon/160000$ only under $$\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000\cdot2^{40}\Lambda}\left(\frac dp\right)^{1/2}.$$ Thus component localization inside the existing cardinality-based architecture does not reach exponent $1-o(1)$.

nodes.label: Universal-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: This forces the decode alternative in `E2E-07`; it does not obstruct soundness.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p\ge103$ and $2\le K\le p/(100\log p)$ there is a legal constant-label table with $1/(2K)\le\epsilon\le2/K$ such that every line family reaching half of every accepted line has $$|R|\ge\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon},$$ while one constant polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Modal endpoint obstruction
nodes.notes: The source audit verdict is `revise`, although the verifier judged this individual construction valid.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For $d=101$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, let $$r_p=\left\lfloor\frac{\log p}{4\log\log p}\right\rfloor.$$ There is a valid table satisfying $$\frac{r_p}{130p}\le\epsilon\le\frac{50r_p}{p},
\qquad \operatorname{Agr}_{101}(f)<\frac2p.$$

nodes.label: Exact-linear endpoint
nodes.notes: Refuted at the legal ambient degree $d=101$; the fixed-$\eta$ target remains compatible with `E2E-23`.
nodes.statement_markdown: There exist absolute $C,c>0$ such that every legal instance with $$\epsilon\ge C\frac dp$$ satisfies $\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c\epsilon$.

nodes.label: Bounded-factor sufficient interface
nodes.notes: This imports the stronger shared incidence proposal `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY`.
nodes.statement_markdown: If the relation alternative in `E2E-07` is strengthened to $D\le K_\theta d$, then $s\le K_\theta$. Hence some factor class has mass at least $e(G_1)/K_\theta=\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$, and the parameter gate makes its mass times $p+1$ exceed $4\Delta_i$. Under this stronger interface, the factor alternative of `E2E-14` follows by pigeonhole.

summary: Round 1 supplies a complete conditional KTZ-style DAG. Exact accepted evidence covers weighted interpolation, reached-root extension, characteristic-safe cleanup, simple roots, and component-level recovery of one polynomial. Near-linear closure requires two new structural inputs: a label-aware rank-or-decode lemma producing a relation of weighted degree $D\le A_\theta d\epsilon^{-\theta/(1-\theta)}\ll\epsilon p$, and a heavy-factor-or-decoder lemma collapsing the resulting factor list. A high-direction simple root would then linearize one irreducible factor as $Z-Q$, allowing all of its edges across disconnected components to charge directly to one $Q$ and avoiding the $p^{-1/2}$ Vinh floor. The stronger shared incidence interface $D=O_\theta(d)$ would make factor concentration automatic. The fixed-$\eta$ target remains blocked; the exact exponent-one endpoint is separately refuted by the modal construction.
target_statement: Prove that soundness at least $(d/p)^{1-o(1)}$ yields agreement with one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial for $100<d<p$ over $\mathbb F_p$.
title: End-to-end soundness chain
